title_en: Inside the old gas pipeline where Ukraine is fighting an underground war with Russia
title_zh: 在旧天然气管道内，乌克兰正在与俄罗斯进行地下战争
summary: Watch: The BBC's Jonathan Beale joins Ukrainian forces taking the battle below ground and out of sight of Russian drones.
summary_zh: 观看：BBC 的乔纳森·比尔 (Jonathan Beale) 与乌克兰军队一起在地下、俄罗斯无人机看不见的地方进行战斗。
body_en: Inside the gas pipeline where Ukraine is fighting an underground war with Russia - BBC News
For the past seven months Ukrainian forces have been living and fighting Russian troops in an old Soviet gas pipeline in the Kharkiv region.
The BBC is the first international broadcaster to enter the pipeline where this subterranean battle is taking place.

With a diameter of just over a metre there's enough room only to crawl. But it is relatively safe from the drones that now saturate the skies above the front line – and which are making it nigh-on impossible for either side to advance.
The BBC's defence correspondent Jonathan Beale reports from near Kupyansk, where he went underground with the 13th Khartiia Operational Brigade.
Read Jonathan Beale's dispatch from the front line.
body_zh: 乌克兰与俄罗斯在天然气管道内进行地下战争 - BBC 新闻
在过去的七个月里，乌克兰军队一直在哈尔科夫地区的一条旧苏联天然气管道中与俄罗斯军队作战。
BBC 是第一家进入这场地下战斗发生地的国际广播公司。
直径只有一米多一点，空间足够爬行。但对于无人机来说，它相对安全，无人机现在充斥着前线上方的天空，这使得双方几乎不可能前进。
BBC 防务记者乔纳森·比尔 (Jonathan Beale) 在库皮扬斯克 (Kupyansk) 附近进行报道，他在那里与第 13 哈蒂亚作战旅一起进入地下。
阅读乔纳森·比尔在前线发来的快报。

title_en: Israeli military launches rare ground operation in Gaza beyond Yellow Line
title_zh: 以色列军队在黄线以外的加沙地带发起罕见的地面行动
summary: Hamas condemns the incursion, which the Israeli military says is dismantling a "terror tunnel", as a "flagrant" ceasefire violation.
summary_zh: 哈马斯谴责这次入侵，以色列军方称这次入侵正在拆除“恐怖隧道”，这是“公然”违反停火协议。
body_en: Israeli ground forces have launched a rare operation in part of the central Gaza Strip outside their control, after issuing evacuation orders for residents.
Witnesses said tanks advanced east of Nuseirat refugee camp and rolled onto the territory's main north to south road under the cover of artillery strikes.
The Israeli military said the "targeted" operation aimed to dismantle a "terror tunnel" west of the so-called Yellow Line, which marks the more than 60% of Gaza's territory occupied by Israel.
The Palestinian armed group Hamas, which controls the rest of Gaza, accused Israel of a "flagrant violation" of the October 2025 ceasefire agreement.
Violence has continued in Gaza over the past 13 months, with near-daily Israeli strikes, and living conditions for the 2.1 million people there remain dire.

Early on Wednesday afternoon, Israeli military body Cogat's Arabic spokesperson announced the start of the incursion and warned Palestinians living in an area north of Nuseirat and Bureij refugee camp to stay away for their own safety.
It also said a section of the north to south Salah al-Din road that passed through the area would be closed to traffic.

Later, the Israel Defense Forces (IDF) said it had begun a joint operation with the Shin Bet security service "to dismantle a terror tunnel west of the Yellow Line that posed an immediate and direct threat to IDF troops".

"IDF troops under the Southern Command are deployed in the area in accordance with the ceasefire agreement and will continue to operate to remove any immediate threat and thwart attempts by the Hamas terrorist organisation to harm Israeli civilians or IDF troops, or to violate the agreement," it added.

Hamas warned in a statement that the advance of Israeli military vehicles beyond the Yellow Line and the evacuation of residents constituted "a dangerous development and a flagrant violation of the ceasefire agreement".
Footage published by Palestinian media outlets and on social media showed families fleeing areas near Nuseirat camp following the announcement.

In one video verified by BBC Verify, a man can be seen ducking after hearing artillery fire and then running along Salah al-Din road, about 1.5km (0.9 miles) west of the Yellow Line. "The Israeli occupation now is firing randomly near the houses and tents of people," he says.
Automatic gunfire can be heard in another video filmed just to the south-east.

A resident of Nuseirat who was forced to flee told BBC Arabic's Middle East Daily programme: "The situation is now extremely dire, with Israeli forces firing indiscriminately at areas where displaced people have sought shelter."
"We couldn't take any of our belongings with us - not even our blankets, pillows, or clothes. We had no choice but to leave everything behind."
A second resident also reported "indiscriminate gunfire and shelling" and said there had been "numerous casualties, including fatalities".
Asked about reported fatalities, the IDF sent a general statement about the operation.
Israel building new land barriers in Gaza and displacing families
Israel moves Yellow Line deeper into Gaza, satellite images show
Gaza's Hamas-run Civil Defence agency said three people were killed and others were wounded in three separate Israeli drone strikes on Wednesday.
body_zh: 以色列地面部队在向居民发出疏散命令后，在其控制范围之外的加沙地带中部部分地区发起了罕见的行动。
目击者称，坦克在炮火掩护下向努塞拉特难民营以东推进，驶上该领土从北向南的主要道路。
以色列军方表示，这次“有针对性”行动的目的是拆除所谓黄线以西的一条“恐怖隧道”，黄线标志着加沙60%以上的领土被以色列占领。
控制加沙其他地区的巴勒斯坦武装组织哈马斯指责以色列“公然违反”2025年10月停火协议。
过去 13 个月里，加沙的暴力事件持续不断，以色列几乎每天都会发动袭击，那里 210 万人的生活条件仍然十分悲惨。
周三下午早些时候，以色列军事机构 Cogat 的阿拉伯语发言人宣布开始入侵，并警告居住在 Nuseirat 和 Bureij 难民营以北地区的巴勒斯坦人为了自身安全而远离。
它还表示，穿过该地区的从北到南的 Salah al-Din 公路的一段路段将封闭。
随后，以色列国防军（IDF）表示，已开始与辛贝特安全部门开展联合行动，“拆除黄线以西的一条恐怖隧道，该隧道对以色列国防军部队构成直接威胁”。
声明补充说：“南方司令部领导下的以色列国防军部队根据停火协议部署在该地区，并将继续采取行动消除任何直接威胁，并挫败哈马斯恐怖组织伤害以色列平民或以色列国防军部队或违反协议的企图。”
哈马斯在一份声明中警告说，以色列军车越过黄线和疏散居民构成“危险的事态发展，公然违反停火协议”。
巴勒斯坦媒体和社交媒体发布的视频显示，消息公布后，许多家庭逃离努塞拉特难民营附近的地区。
在 BBC verify 核实的一段视频中，可以看到一名男子在听到炮火声后躲开，然后沿着黄线以西约 1.5 公里（0.9 英里）处的 Salah al-Din 路奔跑。 “以色列占领者现在在人们的房屋和帐篷附近随机开火，”他说。
在东南部拍摄的另一段视频中可以听到自动枪声。
一名被迫逃离的努塞拉特居民告诉BBC阿拉伯语中东日报节目：“现在的局势极其严峻，以色列军队向流离失所者寻求庇护的地区不分青红皂白地开火。”
“我们无法带走任何物品，甚至连毯子、枕头或衣服都不能带走。我们别无选择，只能把所有东西都抛在脑后。”
另一位居民也报告了“不分青红皂白的枪声和炮击”，并表示“造成多人伤亡，包括死亡”。
当被问及报告的死亡人数时，以色列国防军发表了有关此次行动的一般性声明。

title_en: Crimean Bridge attacked again, Russian official says
title_zh: 俄罗斯官员称克里米亚大桥再次遭到袭击
summary: The head of Crimea said traffic was suspended after another attack on the link between Russia and the occupied territory.
summary_zh: 克里米亚领导人表示，俄罗斯与被占领土之间的线路再次遭到袭击后，交通中断。
body_en: Putin's Crimean Bridge comes under attack again, Russian official says - BBC News
The Crimean Bridge has been attacked by Ukraine for the third time this week, a Russian official has said.
The Moscow-installed head of Crimea, Sergei Aksyonov, confirmed that traffic was temporarily suspended following another strike on the bridge connecting Russia to occupied Crimea.
The critical bridge had already been hit twice earlier in the week resulting in severe damage and part of the bridge collapsing into the water.
The important infrastructure has long been targeted by Ukraine because of its significance as a logistical and symbolic asset to Moscow's war effort.
It comes as Russian President Vladimir Putin meets US President Donald Trump and China's President Xi Jinping on Thursday for landmark talks in China .
Aksyonov confirmed the strike on the bridge in the early hours of Thursday via Telegram, adding that assessment of the damage was under way.
Meanwhile, Ukrainian sources have continued to issue air raid alert warnings overnight for districts just outside of the capital Kyiv.

At least three people were killed in a Russian drone attack on Odesa on Wednesday, according to the regional state administration. Officials described the attack as "brutal and deliberate... directly targeting people and their lives".
President Volodymyr Zelensky has called the initial strikes on the Crimean Bridge as an "unprecedented operation" weeks in the making.
Putin's Crimean Bridge partly collapses as Zelensky hails 'unprecedented' attack by Ukraine
Ukraine used drones and missiles against it on 17 November which brought down a key section of the road.
That section of the double-arched, 12-mile bridge now lies on the seabed, brought down by an arsenal of Ukrainian long-range weaponry in a seven-stage operation culminating in a dramatic collapse.
In response, Kremlin spokesman Dmitry Peskov has said the bridge "will be rebuilt, and it will be even better than before".

While Ukrainian forces have struggled to close the bridge for good, recent attempts have brought them closer to destroying the bridge's crucial road and rail route for Russian soldiers heading towards the front line.
Russian forces have also targeted key bridge crossings over the Dnipro River in Kyiv in recent days.
Russian strikes hit the Pivnichnyi (Northern) and Pivdennyi (Southern) bridges causing traffic closures, partial damage to the metro system and some power and water outages.

body_zh: 俄罗斯官员称普京克里米亚大桥再次遭受袭击 -_澳门赌博平台
俄罗斯官员表示，克里米亚大桥本周已是乌克兰第三次袭击。
莫斯科任命的克里米亚领导人谢尔盖·阿克肖诺夫(Sergei Aksyonov)证实，在连接俄罗斯与被占领克里米亚的桥梁再次遭到袭击后，交通暂时中断。
本周早些时候，这座关键的桥梁已遭受两次撞击，造成严重损坏，部分桥梁塌入水中。
这一重要的基础设施长期以来一直是乌克兰的目标，因为它作为莫斯科战争努力的后勤和象征性资产具有重要意义。
俄罗斯总统弗拉基米尔·普京周四在中国会见美国总统唐纳德·特朗普和中国国家主席习近平，进行具有里程碑意义的会谈。
阿克肖诺夫于周四凌晨通过 Telegram 证实了桥梁遭受的袭击，并补充说正在评估损失情况。
与此同时，乌克兰消息人士连夜继续向首都基辅郊外的地区发出空袭警报。
据地区国家管理局称，周三俄罗斯无人机袭击敖德萨，造成至少三人死亡。官员们称这次袭击是“残酷且蓄意的……直接针对人民及其生命”。
总统弗拉基米尔·泽伦斯基称，对克里米亚大桥的最初袭击是一场酝酿数周的“史无前例的行动”。
泽伦斯基称赞乌克兰“史无前例”的袭击，普京的克里米亚大桥部分倒塌
11 月 17 日，乌克兰使用无人机和导弹对其进行攻击，摧毁了该公路​​的一个关键路段。
这座 12 英里长的双拱桥的这一部分现在位于海底，在七阶段行动中被乌克兰远程武器库击落，最终导致戏剧性的倒塌。
作为回应，克里姆林宫发言人德米特里·佩斯科夫表示，这座桥“将被重建，而且会比以前更好”。
虽然乌克兰军队一直在努力永久关闭这座桥，但最近的尝试使他们更接近摧毁这座桥对前往前线的俄罗斯士兵来说至关重要的道路和铁路。
俄罗斯军队最近几天还瞄准了基辅第聂伯河上的主要桥梁。
俄罗斯的袭击袭击了皮夫尼奇尼（北部）和皮夫登尼（南部）桥梁，造成交通堵塞、地铁系统部分损坏以及部分电力和供水中断。

title_en: Russian arrested for spying on US defence company Palantir over Ukraine support
title_zh: 俄罗斯人因对乌克兰支持的美国国防公司 Palantir 进行间谍活动而被捕
summary: The suspect followed employees and was found with fake US IDs and two Russian passports, prosecutors say.
summary_zh: 检察官称，嫌疑人跟踪员工，被发现持有假美国身份证和两本俄罗斯护照。
body_en: A Russian man has been arrested in California's Silicon Valley for allegedly attempting to spy on employees of a technology and defence firm that supports the Ukrainian military.

Igor D'iu is accused of acting as an agent of a foreign government to conduct a covert operation in Palo Alto, near San Francisco. The BBC understands that the company targeted was Palantir Technologies.
D'iu is also charged with stalking employees and possessing falsified identity documents.
The company is not named in charging documents, but is described as a publicly traded technology and defence company that produces software used by Ukraine in its war with Russia.

"The allegations in this case describe a state-sponsored operation to target and harass employees of an American technology and defense company because of that company's assistance to Ukraine in its war with Russia," said US Attorney for the Northern District of California Craig Missakian.
"We will not tolerate any efforts - by foreign governments or otherwise - to turn Silicon Valley into a base for foreign intelligence operations."
Prosecutors say that D'iu entered the US unlawfully via the Mexico border, after travelling there from Istanbul in June.

He was allegedly recruited through the Telegram encrypted messaging app. His handlers referred to Russia as "'the Motherland' and directed D'iu to gather information about the company because it was supplying weapons used against Russia in Ukraine".
On their instruction, he purchased computers, phones, wireless networking equipment and remote access software - tools he needed for his spy mission.
He then went to a coffee shop located near the company's offices in Palo Alto, where he photographed laptop screens of employees who were working there.

His handlers also allegedly "instructed him to position his laptop at designated locations near the company so they could remotely access it and attempt to collect information from company employees in the vicinity".
A source in the industry confirmed that Palantir was targeted, and added that the operation did not penetrate the company's private systems.
They added that the company has been "targeted extensively" by Russia over its involvement in Ukraine, and that the attacks are becoming "increasingly aggressive".
The source, who did not want to be named, said that this was the first time a Russian operative was found while on US soil attempting to spy on the company.
"I think the surprising thing is that they decided to take the risk of sending someone to the US," they said, in an attempt to get into the system "physically".
Palantir has not issued a statement in reaction to the charges.
D'iu also allegedly conducted surveillance of employees and their residences.

On 3 September, he followed a vehicle driven by one senior executive for nearly 30 miles. He fled after she drove to a police station. Police later obtained evidence that he had followed other employees' cars on previous days.
During the investigation, officials discovered identity cards that had been falsified - including a US passport, California ID card, and a Social Security card with the fake name "Hugo Landry Johns".

A raid on his home in October in East Palo Alto turned up two Russian passports, and a handwritten notebook that contained numerous home addresses of employees "family members' names, educational and employment histories, and assessments of their strengths and weaknesses", prosecutors say.
body_zh: 一名俄罗斯男子因涉嫌试图监视一家支持乌克兰军方的技术和国防公司的员工而在加州硅谷被捕。
伊戈尔·迪乌 (Igor D'iu) 被指控充当外国政府特工，在旧金山附近的帕洛阿尔托进行秘密行动。 BBC 了解到，目标公司是 Palantir Technologies。
D'iu 还被指控跟踪员工和拥有伪造的身份证件。
指控文件中没有提到该公司的名字，但被描述为一家上市技术和国防公司，生产乌克兰在与俄罗斯的战争中使用的软件。
加州北区联邦检察官克雷格·米萨基安 (Craig Missakian) 表示：“本案中的指控描述了一项由国家资助的行动，旨在针对和骚扰一家美国技术和国防公司的员工，因为该公司在乌克兰与俄罗斯的战争中向乌克兰提供援助。”
“我们不会容忍任何外国政府或其他方面将硅谷变成外国情报行动基地的行为。”
检察官称，D'iu 六月从伊斯坦布尔前往美国，并通过墨西哥边境非法进入美国。
据称他是通过 Telegram 加密消息应用程序招募的。他的上司将俄罗斯称为“‘祖国’，并指示 D'iu 收集有关该公司的信息，因为该公司在乌克兰供应用于对抗俄罗斯的武器”。
根据他们的指示，他购买了电脑、电话、无线网络设备和远程访问软件——他执行间谍任务所需的工具。
然后，他去了位于帕洛阿尔托的公司办公室附近的一家咖啡店，在那里拍摄了在那里工作的员工的笔记本电脑屏幕。
据称，他的管理人员还“指示他将笔记本电脑放置在公司附近的指定位置，以便他们可以远程访问它并尝试从附近的公司员工那里收集信息”。
一位业内消息人士证实 Palantir 成为目标，并补充说该操作并未渗透到该公司的私人系统。
他们补充说，该公司因参与乌克兰事务而成为俄罗斯“广泛攻击的目标”，而且攻击正变得“越来越激进”。
这位不愿透露姓名的消息人士表示，这是第一次发现俄罗斯特工在美国境内试图监视该公司。
他们说：“我认为令人惊讶的是，他们决定冒险派人去美国”，试图“亲自”进入该系统。
Palantir 尚未针对这些指控发表声明。
据称，D'iu 还对员工及其住所进行监视。
9 月 3 日，他跟随一名高级管理人员驾驶的车辆行驶了近 30 英里。她开车到警察局后，他逃跑了。警方后来获得的证据表明，他前几天曾跟踪其他员工的汽车。
在调查过程中，官员发现了伪造的身份证件，包括美国护照、加州身份证和假名“Hugo Landry Johns”的社会保障卡。
检察官称，10月份对他位于东帕洛阿尔托的家进行搜查，发现了两本俄罗斯护照和一本手写笔记本，其中包含大量员工的家庭住址、“家庭成员的姓名、教育和就业经历以及对他们的优势和劣势的评估”。

title_en: Kuwait says it repelled first Iranian attack in two months after US strikes island
title_zh: 科威特表示，在美国袭击该岛后，它击退了伊朗两个月内的首次袭击
summary: Bahrain says it was also attacked by Iran following a US air strike on the Iranian island of Qeshm in the Gulf on Tuesday.
summary_zh: 巴林表示，美国周二对海湾地区的伊朗格什姆岛发动空袭后，巴林也遭到了伊朗的袭击。
body_en: Kuwait and Bahrain have said they repelled Iranian air attacks overnight as hostilities between Iran and the United States rise.

The drone attack on Kuwait was the first in more than two months. The Iranian army said it had targeted the Ali Al Salem Airbase, which hosts US forces, but Kuwaiti authorities did not report any damage.
It came after US warplanes struck an Iranian missile launch site on Qeshm Island in the Strait of Hormuz, according to US military officials.
Meanwhile, the United Arab Emirates' state oil firm said a crew member was missing after one of its tankers was attacked in the Gulf waterway on Tuesday.
The recent exchanges of fire, as well as deadlock in negotiations on a peace deal, have raised fears of a major escalation in the nine-month-old war.
The conflict began when the US and Israel attacked Iran in late February.
Since then, Iran has retaliated for US and Israeli strikes by launching missiles and drones at Israel and Gulf Arab states hosting US military assets and personnel.
It has also attacked dozens of commercial vessels in and around the Strait of Hormuz, through which a fifth of global oil and gas shipments usually pass.
Pakistani man sentenced to 27 years for Iran-backed plot to kill Trump
Trump says US taking 'very seriously' any Iranian plot against Washington
Iran targets US military base in Bahrain with drone attack
On Tuesday night, Kuwait's military said its air defences engaged "drone threats" but did not report any casualties or damage.

The Kuwaiti foreign ministry condemned the attack, saying it "flagrantly violated Kuwait's sovereignty, directly threatened its security and stability, and constituted a grave breach of international law".

"The explosions seemed to be coming from far away, but hearing them again after a period of calm was both surprising and worrying," Hani Mohammed, an Egyptian resident of Kuwait, told AFP news agency.
Bahrain's military also said on Wednesday that its air defence systems had "intercepted and destroyed several Iranian aerial attacks".
The island kingdom, which hosts the US Navy's 5th Fleet, has reported four attacks over the past six days, following a two-month lull.

Qatar, which has mediated in the stalled indirect talks between Iran and the US, said the Iranian attacks on its neighbours were a "dangerous escalation that threatens to complicate efforts aimed at containing tensions".
The Iranian army said its drones had targeted US Patriot air defence systems and drone and missile launch platforms at Ali Al Salem Air Base in Kuwait.
Later, the army's commander-in-chief, Maj Gen Amir Hatami, warned the US and its allies that it would respond more forcefully to any new attacks on Iran.
"If the enemy repeats its mistake... we have the readiness and the plans to confront it and its supporters in a stronger, more crushing way and without geographic limitations," he said.

title_en: Fears grow that US will put Nobel-winning judge under sanctions after Myanmar genocide ruling
title_zh: 缅甸种族灭绝裁决后，人们越来越担心美国将制裁诺贝尔奖获得者法官
summary: A ruling against Myanmar could set precedent for court’s judgment on Israel’s actions in Gaza Fears are growing that the US could impose sanctions on judges at the international court of justice, including this year’s Nobel peace prize winner, Navi Pillay , if
summary_zh: 对缅甸的裁决可能为法院对以色列在加沙行动的判决开创先例 人们越来越担心美国可能对缅甸实施制裁
body_en: A ruling against Myanmar could set precedent for court’s judgment on Israel’s actions in Gaza

Fears are growing that the US could impose sanctions on judges at the international court of justice, including this year’s Nobel peace prize winner, Navi Pillay , if the court rules on Thursday that the Myanmar government committed genocide against the Rohingya.
‘They showed no mercy’: mapping the Rohingya villages being erased by rebel forces

The ICJ has never found a state responsible for committing genocide, and a significant factor in previous cases has been how to prove “intent” in a crime defined as acts committed with the “intent to destroy, in whole or in part” a national, ethnical, racial or religious group.

Lawyers representing Rohingya survivors say patterns of behaviour by Myanmar’s military, including killing people as they fled, show clear attempts to destroy the group during assaults on Rakhine state in 2016 and 2017.

It is the role of independent judges to interpret the genocide convention. However, judges at the court have taken advice on how to protect their assets from potential US sanctions, as a genocide ruling could be interpreted by Washington as lowering the “legal threshold” for the crime.
The Foundation for Defense of Democracies, an influential thinktank close to the White House, has predicted a genocide ruling will lead to the US imposing sanctions on the ICJ.

The US and Israel fear the final judgment may clarify how to establish a government’s intent to commit a genocide, and so set a precedent that makes it more likely the court will later rule that Israel committed genocide in Gaza.
Myanmar, which has denied carrying out a genocide, claims its actions targeted a military uprising by insurgents.

The ICJ, sometimes described as the UN’s top court, is responsible for settling interstate disputes, unlike the international criminal court (ICC), which prosecutes individuals accused of war crimes and other international crimes.

The US has already imposed crippling sanctions on judges at the ICC after the court issued arrest warrants against the Israeli prime minister, Benjamin Netanyahu. The US has also announced sanctions against the entire ICC as an institution, which it described as a “rogue court”. Washington fears the ICC could go after US troops.

The Gambia, as a litigant, was entitled to appoint an ad hoc judge in the case against Myanmar and chose the South African lawyer Pillay, who in October was awarded the Nobel peace prize . She is required to act as a jurist and not an advocate for the Gambia.
Mike Waltz, the US ambassador to the UN, has sent a warning shot to Pillay and the 15 ICJ judges, saying Washington “will not allow globalist, faux judges to weaponise the law against our troops”.

Waltz asserted last month: “The ICJ ad hoc judge Navi Pillay is tipping the scales on the ICJ’s current proceedings on Myanmar, intending to lower the legal threshold for proving genocide so that weakened and false standard can later be weaponised against American and allied soldiers whenever they raise a finger against terrorists that hide behind civilians.”
In remarks addressed to Pillay, he said: “We see your agenda and we’ll be watching the ICJ’s handling of these proceedings very closely.”

In a speech last Friday, the US secretary of state, Marco Rubio , said: “For this global elite, international law … is an instrument to advance their interests under the pretence of universal principles.”
He warned the ICC against quoting laws to “men with swords”.

Israel has previously criticised adverse advisory opinions issued by the ICJ and refused to implement 2024 orders requiring Israel to admit more aid into Gaza , and to cooperate with Unrwa, the UN relief and works agency.

In the Myanmar case, a 24-page submission jointly filed by the UK and five other mainly European states, argued that the ICJ, in judging intent to commit genocide, should examine a range of “facts and circumstances” assessed “comprehensively and holistically”.
body_zh: 对缅甸不利的裁决可能为法院对以色列在加沙的行动作出判决奠定先例
人们越来越担心，如果国际法院周四裁定缅甸政府对罗兴亚人实施种族灭绝，美国可能会对国际法院的法官实施制裁，其中包括今年的诺贝尔和平奖获得者纳维·皮莱。
“他们毫不留情”：绘制被叛军摧毁的罗辛亚村庄地图
国际法院从未发现一个国家应对种族灭绝负责，而在以往的案件中，一个重要因素是如何证明犯罪的“意图”，该犯罪被定义为“意图全部或部分摧毁”一个民族、民族、种族或宗教团体。
代表罗兴亚幸存者的律师表示，缅甸军方的行为模式，包括在逃亡时杀人，表明在 2016 年和 2017 年袭击若开邦期间，明显企图摧毁该组织。
解释种族灭绝公约是独立法官的职责。然而，法院法官就如何保护其资产免受美国潜在制裁的影响听取了建议，因为华盛顿可能将种族灭绝裁决解释为降低了犯罪的“法律门槛”。
接近白宫的有影响力的智囊团捍卫民主基金会预测，种族灭绝裁决将导致美国对国际法院实施制裁。
美国和以色列担心最终判决可能会澄清如何确定政府实施种族灭绝的意图，因此开创了一个先例，使法院稍后更有可能裁定以色列在加沙实施种族灭绝。
缅甸否认实施种族灭绝，声称其行动是针对叛乱分子的军事起义。
国际法院有时被称为联合国最高法院，负责解决国家间争端，这与起诉被控犯有战争罪和其他国际罪行的个人的国际刑事法院（ICC）不同。
在国际刑事法院对以色列总理本杰明·内塔尼亚胡发出逮捕令后，美国已经对国际刑事法院的法官实施了严厉的制裁。美国还宣布对整个国际刑事法院作为一个机构实施制裁，称其为“流氓法院”。华盛顿担心国际刑事法院可能会追捕美军。
冈比亚作为诉讼当事人，有权在针对缅甸的案件中任命一名专案法官，并选择了10月获得诺贝尔和平奖的南非律师皮莱。她被要求担任法学家，而不是冈比亚的辩护人。
美国驻联合国大使迈克·沃尔兹（Mike Waltz）向皮莱和国际法院的 15 名法官发出警告，称华盛顿“不会允许全球主义的假法官将法律武器化来对付我们的军队”。
沃尔兹上个月断言：“国际法院专案法官纳维·皮莱正在改变国际法院目前对缅甸的诉讼程序，意在降低证明种族灭绝的法律门槛，以便以后每当美国和盟军士兵对隐藏在平民背后的恐怖分子发动袭击时，就会用削弱和错误的标准来对付他们。”
他在对皮莱的讲话中说：“我们看到了你们的议程，我们将密切关注国际法院对这些诉讼程序的处理。”
美国国务卿马可·卢比奥在上周五的一次演讲中表示：“对于这些全球精英来说，国际法……是在普遍原则的幌子下促进他们利益的工具。”
他警告国际刑事法院不要向“持剑之人”引用法律。
以色列此前曾批评国际法院发表的不利咨询意见，并拒绝执行2024年命令，要求以色列允许更多援助进入加沙，并与联合国救济和工程机构近东救济工程处合作。
在缅甸案中，英国和其他五个主要欧洲国家联合提交了一份长达24页的意见书，认为国际法院在判断种族灭绝意图时，应该审查一系列“全面、整体”评估的“事实和情况”。

title_en: Myanmar faces historic genocide verdict at UN court over Rohingya massacres
title_zh: 缅甸因罗兴亚人大屠杀面临联合国法庭历史性种族灭绝判决
summary: No state has ever been found guilty by an international court of committing genocide.
summary_zh: 国际法庭从未判定任何国家犯有种族灭绝罪。
body_en: When the judges of the International Court of Justice read out their verdict in the seven-year-old genocide case filed by The Gambia against Myanmar on Thursday, they could make history.

In the years since the Genocide Convention was signed in 1948, after the Nazi Holocaust, dozens of individuals have been successfully prosecuted for the crime of genocide, in conflicts such as those in Rwanda and the former Yugoslavia.
But no state has ever been found guilty by an international court of committing genocide.

"It would be a judgment of landmark importance if The Gambia were to win this case," says Arsalan Suleman, the lawyer leading the case against Myanmar at the court. "It would give renewed vitality to the 1948 Genocide Convention and to the notion of international legal accountability for crimes committed by a state."
The mass expulsion of the Rohingya population of Rakhine State in August and September 2017 was without question a military operation of exceptional brutality.

I was among a very small number of journalists who witnessed the deliberate burning of Rohingya villages in Rakhine, and also the dreadful human suffering of the hundreds of thousands who fled to neighbouring Bangladesh.
Their accounts of killing, torture and mass rape by Burmese soldiers have been thoroughly documented by human rights groups and a United Nations fact-finding mission , external .

I have on many occasions interviewed ethnic Rakhine people about their animosity towards the Muslim population, and I have documented the systematic obliteration of what remained of Rohingya villages by the Myanmar state.
But the question posed at the UN's top court, the ICJ, is whether all of this amounted to genocide.

The ICJ was established in 1945 to help settle disputes between states, not to try international crimes. However, it was chosen to address the attacks on Rohingyas in Myanmar because there were few other avenues of redress for the victims.

Myanmar authorities have denied accusations of ethnic cleansing or genocide, saying they were only responding to terrorist actions by Rohingya militants with so-called military "clearance operations".

A UN report in 2018 , based on hundreds of interviews, said the army's tactics were "grossly disproportionate to actual security threats". It said top military figures in Myanmar must be investigated for genocide in Rakhine State and crimes against humanity in other areas. Myanmar rejected the report.
As Myanmar was not a signatory to the International Criminal Court, it was not possible to file a case there against the officials accused of atrocities in Rakhine State.

Instead in November 2019 The Gambia, backed by the Organisation of Islamic Co-operation, filed a case at the ICJ, arguing that all states are bound by the Genocide Convention, so all have an interest in upholding it.
It accused the state in Myanmar, not just the military, of genocide.

This was a novelty in international law; a state not directly affected by an act, arguing that it had legal standing to make a complaint because it was indirectly affected by any violations of such an important convention.
Myanmar objected to this argument, but the ICJ judges ruled that The Gambia was eligible to file the case.

The case drew even more attention when the Nobel laureate Aung San Suu Kyi, who at the time headed the elected government in Myanmar, chose to lead the initial legal defence of her country at The Hague in person, for which she was widely criticised.

She had very limited influence over the actions of the Myanmar military in Rakhine State, but her refusal to condemn them dismayed many of those who until then had admired her courage and adherence to democratic principles.
Since she was deposed by a coup in 2021 and placed under arrest the defence has been led by a new team appointed by the military.
body_zh: 当国际法院法官周四宣读冈比亚诉缅甸长达七年的种族灭绝案的判决时，他们可以创造历史。
自1948年签署《种族灭绝公约》以来，纳粹大屠杀之后，已有数十人在卢旺达和前南斯拉夫等冲突中因种族灭绝罪被成功起诉。
但国际法庭从未判定任何国家犯有种族灭绝罪。
“如果冈比亚赢得此案，这将是具有里程碑意义的判决，”在法庭上负责缅甸案件的律师阿萨兰·苏莱曼 (Arsalan Suleman) 说。 “它将为 1948 年《种族灭绝公约》以及对国家所犯罪行承担国际法律责任的概念注​​入新的活力。”
2017 年 8 月和 9 月大规模驱逐若开邦罗兴亚人无疑是一次极其残暴的军事行动。
我是极少数亲眼目睹若开邦罗兴亚人村庄被蓄意焚烧的记者之一，也目睹了数十万人逃往邻国孟加拉国所遭受的可怕苦难。
他们对缅甸士兵杀害、酷刑和大规模强奸的描述已被人权组织和联合国外部实况调查团详细记录。
我曾多次采访若开族人民，了解他们对穆斯林人口的敌意，我还记录了缅甸政府对罗兴亚村庄剩余部分的系统性消灭。
但联合国最高法院国际法院提出的问题是，这一切是否构成种族灭绝。
国际法院成立于 1945 年，旨在帮助解决国家之间的争端，而不是审判国际罪行。然而，选择它来解决缅甸罗辛亚人的袭击问题是因为受害者几乎没有其他补救途径。
缅甸当局否认了种族清洗或种族灭绝的指控，称他们只是通过所谓的军事“清除行动”来回应罗兴亚武装分子的恐怖行动。
联合国 2018 年的一份报告基于数百次采访，称军队的战术“与实际的安全威胁严重不相称”。报告称，必须对缅甸高级军事人物在若开邦的种族灭绝罪和其他地区的反人类罪进行调查。缅甸拒绝接受这份报告。
由于缅甸不是国际刑事法院的签署国，因此无法对被指控在若开邦实施暴行的官员提起诉讼。
相反，冈比亚在伊斯兰合作组织的支持下，于 2019 年 11 月向国际法院提起诉讼，声称所有国家都受到《种族灭绝公约》的约束，因此维护该公约符合所有国家的利益。
它指责缅甸政府，而不仅仅是军方，进行种族灭绝。
这在国际法中是一个新鲜事。未直接受到某项行为影响的国家，声称其具有提出申诉的法律地位，因为它受到任何违反如此重要公约的行为的间接影响。
缅甸反对这一论点，但国际法院法官裁定冈比亚有资格提起诉讼。
当当时领导缅甸民选政府的诺贝尔奖获得者昂山素季选择亲自在海牙领导国家的初步法律辩护时，此案引起了更多关注，她因此受到广泛批评。
她对缅甸军方在若开邦的行动的影响力非常有限，但她拒绝谴责这些行动，这让许多此前钦佩她的勇气和对民主原则的坚持的人感到沮丧。
自 2021 年她被政变废黜并被捕以来，辩方一直由军方任命的新团队领导。

summary_zh: 以色列军方表示，周三已在加沙中部哈马斯控制的地区发起行动，法新社记者在那里看到以色列军队
body_en: The Israeli military said it had launched an operation on Wednesday in a Hamas-controlled area of central Gaza, where an AFP journalist saw Israeli tanks position themselves east of the Nuseirat refugee camp. body_en: Yalta became a byword for betrayal. Will Trump, Xi and Putin enact another carve-up?
That is the question the Guardian’s diplomatic correspondent Patrick Wintour seeks to address in his piece about the expected, Putin, Trump and Xi, meeting at Apec on Thursday.

It is a truism in diplomacy that if you are not around the table, the risk is that you, or your values, are on the menu and about to be carved up. Many excluded from the summit in Shenzhen, principally Ukraine but also eastern Europe and Baltic countries, Taiwan and even Iran, have reason to be nervous that their sponsors might abandon them in a complex geopolitical trade-off that Putin envisions, and Trump seems to endorse.
body_zh: 雅尔塔成为背叛的代名词。特朗普、习近平和普京是否会再次瓜分？
这是《卫报》外交记者帕特里克·温图尔在其关于普京、特朗普和习近平预计将于周四在亚太经合组织会议上会面的文章中试图解决的问题。
外交上有一条不言而喻的道理：如果你不在谈判桌旁，那么你或你的价值观就会出现在菜单上并即将被瓜分的风险。许多被排除在深圳峰会之外的国家，主要是乌克兰，还有东欧和波罗的海国家、台湾，甚至伊朗，都有理由担心他们的赞助商可能会在普京所设想的复杂的地缘政治权衡中放弃他们，而特朗普似乎也支持这种权衡。

title_en: 'The drones don't fly here' - BBC reports from Ukraine's new front line
title_zh: “无人机不会飞到这里”——BBC 来自乌克兰新前线的报道
summary: Ukrainian forces are fighting Russian troops in an old Soviet tunnel in the Kharkiv region.
summary_zh: 乌克兰军队正在哈尔科夫地区的一条旧苏联隧道中与俄罗斯军队作战。
body_en: There's a new front in the war in Ukraine, and it is underground.
For the past seven months Ukrainian forces have been living and fighting Russian troops in an old Soviet gas pipeline in the north-eastern Kharkiv region.

With a diameter of just over a metre there is enough room only to crawl. But it is relatively safe from the drones that now saturate the skies above the front line – and make it nigh-on impossible for either side to advance.
Going underground is now the "only option", says Zanuda, who has helped plan Ukraine's tunnel operation and calls it a new world of fighting. But, he acknowledges, it is hard.
"On the surface you always have some room to manoeuvre, but here you can only engage the enemy head-on."

The journey to get to this subterranean battleground in the Kharkiv region only reinforced the dangers on the ground: a high-speed move by vehicle across open fields, followed by a long march across muddy ground – accompanied by Ukrainian troops with their weapons loaded, ready to shoot down Russian drones.
Arriving at the tunnel entrance, the first thing to hit you is the lingering smell of gas and fetid air.
Both sides use openings in the pipeline to get to the surface, where most of the fighting takes place. They have made breaches in the ground, and used welding tools to break through the thick steel.

The Russians were the first to exploit the pipe to infiltrate the nearby city of Kupyansk in September 2025. They have used underground pipelines before, during the capture of the city of Avdiivka in 2024, and last year in their bid to recapture areas of Russia's Kursk region.
But Ukrainian forces have slowly turned the tables.
A specially designed electric cart transports troops and supplies through the pipeline.

They call it the Kupyansk metro. It occasionally breaks down. We travelled on it for 40 minutes, heads bowed and legs crossed. There is a regular bump as you cross the welded sections of the pipe. It is like an austere fairground ride, without the fun.

Our destination was a break in the pipeline where Ukrainian troops have built dug-outs to store ammunition and equipment, with just enough room to stand. It is where the man they call Musician conducts the movement of troops and supplies. He has been living like a mole, his face engrained with dirt and earth.

Musician tells me he has spent the past three months there, with a few brief visits above ground to clean up or go to the toilet. From time to time we can hear the thuds of artillery rounds above. Musician tells me we are close to the line of contact: "But it's safe underground."
The cart continues its journey into the bowels of the earth. It returns about half an hour later with more troops covered in dirt. They have been fighting in positions on the surface.
There is a look of relief on their dust-caked faces.
"It's more comfortable in the pipe because drones don't fly here, and neither do artillery shells or glide bombs," says Vovochka, who has been fighting on the ground for the past three weeks.

But there has been fighting in the pipeline, too. Operation Veles, named after a mythical Slavic god of the underworld, began in April. Since then Ukraine has advanced 15km (9.3 miles) along the pipeline.
It has been painstaking, backbreaking work – with the ever-present fear of coming into contact with the enemy.

Back above ground we meet a few of the soldiers, from the 13th Khartiia Brigade of Ukraine's National Guard, who have taken part in the mission. Their first task was to clear the detritus, water and Russian barricades inside the pipeline.
body_zh: 乌克兰战争出现了一条新战线，而且是地下战线。
过去七个月里，乌克兰军队一直在哈尔科夫地区东北部的一条旧苏联天然气管道中与俄罗斯军队作战。
直径只有一米多一点，只有爬行的空间。但对于无人机来说，它相对安全，无人机现在充斥着前线上方的天空，使得双方几乎不可能前进。
扎努达说，现在进入地下是“唯一的选择”，他曾帮助规划乌克兰的隧道作业，并将其称为一个新的战斗世界。但是，他承认，这很难。
“表面上你总是有回旋的余地，但在这里你只能与敌人正面交锋。”
前往哈尔科夫地区这个地下战场的旅程只会加剧地面上的危险：车辆在开阔的田野上高速行驶，然后在泥泞的地面上进行长距离行军，而乌克兰军队则携带武器，准备击落俄罗斯无人机。
到达隧道入口，首先映入眼帘的是挥之不去的煤气味和恶臭的空气。
双方都利用管道中的开口到达地面，大部分战斗都是在那里发生的。他们在地面上挖了一个缺口，并使用焊接工具击穿了厚厚的钢材。
俄罗斯人于 2025 年 9 月率先利用该管道渗透到附近的库皮扬斯克市。此前，他们在 2024 年占领阿夫季夫卡市期间以及去年夺回俄罗斯库尔斯克地区的过程中都曾使用过地下管道。
但乌克兰军队已经慢慢扭转了局面。
一辆专门设计的电动车通过管道运输部队和物资。
他们称之为库皮扬斯克地铁。它偶尔会崩溃。我们低着头，盘着腿，在上面走了40分钟。当您穿过管道的焊接部分时，会出现规则的凸起。这就像一次简朴的游乐场之旅，没有乐趣。
我们的目的地是管道中断处，乌克兰军队在那里建造了掩体来储存弹药和装备，只有足够的空间站立。这是被他们称为音乐家的人指挥部队和物资调动的地方。他一直过着像鼹鼠一样的生活，脸上刻满了泥土。
音乐家告诉我，过去三个月他一直在那里度过，并在地面上进行了几次短暂的清洁或上厕所。我们不时能听到上面炮弹的轰鸣声。音乐家告诉我，我们已经接近接触线了：“但地下很安全。”
马车继续前往地球内部。大约半小时后，它回来了，更多的部队被泥土覆盖。他们一直在地表阵地上进行战斗。
他们布满灰尘的脸上露出了如释重负的表情。
“在管道里更舒服，因为无人机不会在这里飞行，炮弹或滑翔炸弹也不会在这里飞行，”过去三周一直在地面作战的沃沃奇卡说。
但战斗也正在酝酿之中。韦莱斯行动于四月开始，以斯拉夫神话中的地狱之神命名。此后乌克兰已沿管道推进了 15 公里（9.3 英里）。
这是一项艰苦、费力的工作，而且始终担心与敌人接触。
回到地面后，我们遇到了一些来自乌克兰国民警卫队第 13 Khartiia 旅的士兵，他们参与了这次任务。他们的首要任务是清除管道内的碎石、水和俄罗斯路障。

title_en: Parents jailed for torture and death of four-year-old girl found along French motorway in 1987
title_zh: 1987 年法国高速公路沿线发现四岁女孩，父母因酷刑致死而入狱
summary: Inass Touloub's body was found along the A10 road in 1987, bearing marks of abuse, and was not identified until 2018.
summary_zh: Inass Touloub 的尸体于 1987 年在 A10 公路沿线被发现，身上有被虐待的痕迹，直到 2018 年才被确认身份。
body_en: Parents jailed for torture and death of four-year-old girl in France nearly 40 years ago - BBC News
The mother of a four-year-old girl killed in central France and found along a motorway almost 40 years ago has been sentenced to 20 years in prison.
Halima El Bakhti, 72, was found guilty on Tuesday of "torture and acts of barbarity resulting in death without the intent to kill", French media reports.
The girl's father, 74-year-old Ahmed Touloub, was handed a 15-year sentence as an accomplice.

Four-year-old Inass Touloub was found along the A10 road in Suèvres in the Loir-et-Cher department on 11 August 1987. Her body bore multiple marks of abuse, including human bite marks, broken bones and burns with an iron.
She was buried in an unmarked grave near the location where her body was found. Unidentified for three decades, she was known only as the "Little Martyr of the A10".
Then, in 2018, she was identified after the DNA of her brother – tested in an unrelated case – matched with hers, leading to the arrest of their parents.
The trial took place in Loir-et-Cher Assize Court from 2 November, with the verdict delivered on Tuesday after several hours of deliberation.

During the trial, prosecutor Anaïs Allio emphasised that "not a single part of Inass's body was spared", and recalled the "sense of vertigo that overcame us all" upon viewing the "unbearable photographs" from the autopsy, France Info reports.
The jury concluded that the child's mother was suffering from impaired judgement at the time of the girl's death, which reduced the maximum potential sentence.
French media outlet France Info described the two defendants as sitting stoically in chairs before the court with their heads bowed as the reasoning behind the verdict was read out.
El Bakhti and Touloub have 10 days to appeal the verdict.
Inass's death sparked one of France's biggest ever investigations, with the girl's photograph posted in public places and an alert sent to more than 30 countries.
body_zh: 近 40 年前，法国四岁女孩的父母因酷刑致死而入狱 - BBC 新闻
大约 40 年前，一名四岁女孩在法国中部被杀，并在高速公路上被发现，她的母亲被判处 20 年监禁。
据法国媒体报道，72 岁的哈利玛·埃尔·巴赫蒂 (Halima El Bakhti) 于周二被判犯有“酷刑和野蛮行为，导致无杀人意图的死亡”罪名。
女孩的父亲，74 岁的艾哈迈德·图卢布 (Ahmed Touloub)，因共犯被判处 15 年徒刑。
1987 年 8 月 11 日，4 岁的伊纳斯·图卢布 (Inass Touloub) 被发现在卢瓦尔-谢尔省苏埃夫尔 (Suèvres) 的 A10 公路上。她的身上有多种虐待痕迹，包括人类咬痕、骨折和熨斗烧伤痕迹。
她被埋葬在尸体被发现地点附近的一个没有标记的坟墓里。三十年来，她身份不明，只被称为“A10小烈士”。
然后，在 2018 年，她哥哥的 DNA 与她的 DNA 相匹配（在一个无关的案件中进行了检测）后，她的身份被确认，导致他们的父母被捕。
审判从 11 月 2 日起在卢瓦谢尔巡回法院进行，经过几个小时的审议后于周二做出判决。
据《法国信息报》报道，在审判过程中，检察官阿纳伊斯·阿利奥强调，“伊纳斯身体的任何一个部位都没有幸免”，并回忆起在看到尸检时“令人难以忍受的照片”时“我们所有人都感到的眩晕感”。
陪审团得出的结论是，女孩死亡时，孩子的母亲判断力受损，因此减少了可能的最高刑期。
法国媒体《France Info》称，在宣读判决背后的理由时，两名被告低着头，坚忍地坐在法庭前的椅子上。
El Bakhti 和 Touloub 有 10 天的时间对判决提出上诉。
伊纳斯之死引发了法国有史以来最大规模的调查之一，该女孩的照片张贴在公共场所，并向 30 多个国家发出了警报。

title_en: Claude-maker Anthropic poised for stock market debut worth up to $1.5tn
title_zh: Claude-maker Anthropic 准备在股市首次亮相，价值高达 1.5 兆美元
summary: Anthropic started just five years ago an is now one of the biggest names in artificial intelligence.
summary_zh: Anthropic 成立于五年前，现已成为人工智能领域最知名的公司之一。
body_en: By Kali Hays , Technology reporter , Samira Hussain , North America business correspondent and Osmond Chia , Business reporter
Anthropic is poised to hit a value of up to $1.5tn (£1.14tn) when its shares start trading on the stock market on Thursday.
The artificial intelligence (AI) company behind the popular chatbot Claude said its shares will be priced at $83 each when it lists on the Nasdaq, a tech-focused stock exchange based in New York.
That price will make it one of the most highly valued companies in the world.

It will be the first US firm focused exclusively on AI to go public, marking a crucial test for the fast-growing industry, which faces questions over whether the huge investment poured into the technology will be profitable.
The AI firm said earlier this month it would likely offer its shares for between $70 and $78 each, which valued the company at up to $1.3tn.

But demand for Anthropic's stock debut - commonly referred to as its initial public offering, or IPO - is very high, according to one early investor in the company who spoke with the BBC on condition of anonymity.
If that turns out to be the case, Anthropic's valuation could quickly blow past its target on Thursday when trading begins.

Depending on how strong that demand is, Anthropic could even exceed the early market valuation of Elon Musk's SpaceX, which was the world's most highly valued stock debut when it went public with a value of $2.2tn in June.
However, in the weeks that followed, SpaceX shares fell significantly in price .

As it stands, Anthropic's listing will see the firm raise more than $68bn from its initial investors. It is also expecting another $26bn from private placements. So the total amount the company will raise is expected to be $94bn.
The amount of cash Anthropic has raised from its listing is already more than SpaceX raised in June .
OpenAI, the maker of ChatGPT and Anthropic's biggest AI rival, is expected to go public next year.

Until then, Anthropic will be the only public company in the US that is entirely focused on the technology, or one that was founded and built around AI tools and products. Its scope is different from tech giants like Google and Microsoft that also develop AI but are involved in other tech services.
The seven Anthropic founders who are about to become multi-billionaires
There is excitement around Anthropic's listing, but also some concern from investors around its ability to generate revenue and profits going forward.

Yang Wang, a principle financial analyst with Counterpoint Research, said the central issue for Anthropic is whether its business "can keep pace" as hundreds of billions of dollars in financial obligations come due in the next couple of years.
"Nevertheless, it is not an everyday occurrence for public investors to gain direct exposure to a frontier-model developer with the potential to shape the next stage of productivity," Wang said.

While nearly every other major tech company is pouring huge amounts of money into the technology and infrastructure required for their own AI tools, they are built around social media or online retail or online search. AI tools and applications are secondary.
"Anthropic going public gives us a whole new window into what AI demand looks like," Marta Norton, who heads strategy at investment firm Empower, told the BBC.
body_zh: 作者：Kali Hays，科技记者，Samira Hussain，北美商业记者和 Osmond Chia，商业记者
当 Anthropic 的股票周四开始在股市交易时，其股价预计将达到 1.5 兆美元（1.14 兆英镑）。
广受欢迎的聊天机器人 Claude 背后的人工智能 (AI) 公司表示，其在纽约纳斯达克上市时的股票定价为每股 83 美元。
这个价格将使其成为世界上估值最高的公司之一。
这将是第一家专门专注于人工智能上市的美国公司，这对这个快速增长的行业来说是一次至关重要的考验，该行业面临着对该技术的巨额投资能否盈利的质疑。
这家人工智能公司本月早些时候表示，可能会以每股 70 至 78 美元的价格发行股票，这使得该公司的估值高达 1.3 兆美元。
但据一位不愿透露姓名的公司早期投资者表示，对 Anthropic 股票首次亮相（通常称为首次公开募股（IPO））的需求非常高。
如果事实果真如此，周四交易开始时，Anthropic 的估值可能会很快超过其目标。
根据需求的强劲程度，Anthropic 甚至可能超过埃隆·马斯克 (Elon Musk) 旗下 SpaceX 的早期市场估值，后者在 6 月份以 2.2 万亿美元的价格上市时，成为全球估值最高的股票。
然而，在接下来的几周里，SpaceX 股价大幅下跌。
按照目前的情况，Anthropic 的上市将使该公司从初始投资者那里筹集超过 680 亿美元。它还预计将通过私募筹集另外 260 亿美元。因此，该公司融资总额预计为 940 亿美元。
Anthropic 上市筹集的现金金额已经超过 SpaceX 6 月份筹集的资金。
ChatGPT 的制造商和 Anthropic 最大的人工智能竞争对手 OpenAI 预计将于明年上市。
在此之前，Anthropic 将成为美国唯一一家完全专注于该技术的上市公司，或者是一家围绕人工智能工具和产品创立和构建的公司。其范围不同于谷歌和微软等科技巨头，后者也开发人工智能，但涉足其他科技服务。
即将成为亿万富翁的七位 Anthropic 创始人
Anthropic 的上市令人兴奋，但投资者也对其未来产生收入和利润的能力感到担忧。
Counterpoint Research 首席财务分析师 Yang Wang 表示，Anthropic 的核心问题是，随着未来几年数千亿美元的财务债务到期，其业务能否“跟上步伐”。
王说：“尽管如此，公众投资者直接投资于有潜力塑造下一阶段生产力的前沿模式开发商的情况并不常见。”
尽管几乎所有其他主要科技公司都在自己的人工智能工具所需的技术和基础设施上投入了大量资金，但它们都是围绕社交媒体或在线零售或在线搜索构建的。人工智能工具和应用程序是次要的。
投资公司 Empower 战略主管玛塔·诺顿 (Marta Norton) 告诉 BBC：“Anthropic 的上市为我们提供了一个了解人工智能需求的全新窗口。”

title_en: Elon Musk says record spending on US midterms was 'pretty foolish'
title_zh: 埃隆·马斯克表示美国中期选举创纪录的支出“非常愚蠢”
summary: The multi-billionaire also said he was "not Maga", distancing himself from the political movement linked to Trump.
summary_zh: 这位亿万富翁还表示，他“不是马加”，与与特朗普有关的政治运动保持距离。
body_en: Elon Musk said on Wednesday that he felt "pretty foolish" about the record sum he spent on the US midterm elections, following sweeping Republican defeats.
The Tesla and SpaceX CEO was the campaign's top individual donor, giving $446m (£339m) to support President Donald Trump's party, particularly in Texas where many of Musk's firms are based.
Musk, who had backed Trump's second White House bid, also said he was "not Maga" - the Make America Great Again movement associated with the president.
Democrats won control of the Senate and House, while Texas, Ohio and other states swung away from Trump, who has faced pressure over the impact his policies have had on the cost of living.
Musk was speaking virtually at the New York Times DealBook Summit, an annual conference hosted in the city attended by major business and political leaders.
"I'm not Maga," Musk said, referring to the right-wing political movement.
He added: "I'm not sure what Maga means... if that means sort of blind adherence to a set of policies by the Republican Party, then I certainly don't have that."
Musk went on to say he did not see much for the money he had spent on the Republicans' campaign, though he added that it was likely that candidates would have fared worse without the spending.

title_en: Former U.S. ambassador on Trump's joint summit with leaders of China and Russia
title_zh: 美国前大使谈特朗普与中国和俄罗斯领导人的联合峰会
summary: NPR's Leila Fadel speaks to Nicholas Burns, former U.S. ambassador to China and NATO, about President Trump's planned meeting with the leaders of China and Russia.
summary_zh: 美国国家公共广播电台 (NPR) 的莱拉·法德尔 (Leila Fadel) 与美国前驻华大使和北约大使尼古拉斯·伯恩斯 (Nicholas Burns) 谈论特朗普总统计划与中国领导人会面的情况
body_en: Former U.S. ambassador on Trump's joint summit with leaders of China and Russia NPR's Leila Fadel speaks to Nicholas Burns, former U.S. ambassador to China and NATO, about President Trump's planned meeting with the leaders of China and Russia.
NPR's Leila Fadel speaks to Nicholas Burns, former U.S. ambassador to China and NATO, about President Trump's planned meeting with the leaders of China and Russia.

Let's turn now to Nicholas Burns. He served as the Biden administration's U.S. ambassador to China and as the U.S. ambassador to NATO under President George W. Bush. He's now an international relations scholar at Harvard University. Good morning, Ambassador. And welcome back to the program.
NICHOLAS BURNS: Good morning, Leila. Thank you.

FADEL: So let's start with the trilateral meeting between Trump, Xi and Russian President Vladimir Putin. What message does it send to U.S. allies to have the three of them appearing together exclusively?

BURNS: Leila, I think that our allies - Japan, South Korea, the Philippines, NATO allies - very worried about this meeting. Here you have the first-ever meeting among President Trump, President Xi and President Putin. And Ukraine's on the agenda - without Ukraine in the room. And I think it's really a major mistake not to have President Zelenskyy there. We can't have a situation in this decade where the fate of a country - Ukraine - is being talked about, maybe even decided about, by three other leaders. And so I think that's a major mistake by the United States to put itself in this position.

The other country that should be at that table is Japan. China and Russia have been engaged in a massive intimidation operation of Japan over the last year - economic boycotts, Russian and Chinese military maneuvers around the Japanese home islands. Japan's our No. 1 ally in Asia - not at the table. So I think the imagery here - and the photo op's going to be a major part of this meeting. It's a short meeting. It's really wrong for the United States. Our allies are so much more important to us than China and Russia.
FADEL: When you say it's a major mistake, what would the consequences of that mistake be?

BURNS: Well, anxiety in ally capitals and loss of confidence in the United States. I think particularly, a lot of people have said this meeting looks somewhat like the Yalta meeting, February 1945 - Stalin, FDR, Churchill deciding the fate of Eastern Europe over the heads of the Eastern Europeans. There are a lot of differences between 81 years ago and now. But the fact that the three very strong countries in the world will be discussing what should happen in Ukraine, when Putin's the aggressor and Zelenskyy is the victim, I think is a major problem for U.S. credibility in the NATO alliance, certainly, and also with the Ukrainians.

FADEL: I wonder, also - I mean, China is hosting here. But there are things that China probably does not want to talk about with the U.S. And that includes this recent concern about spying when it comes to Nvidia. There are tightened export controls on AI chips, as well. How will that affect the meeting between Trump and Xi?

BURNS: Well, you know, that's the elephant in the room, Leila. President Trump has said he's not going to raise it. I'm quite sure President Xi Jinping will not raise it. But certainly, there'll be senior level contacts between the U.S. and China in Shenzhen about what has happened - the allegation of espionage, the fact that China has been trying to acquire - illicitly - American advanced semiconductors for their AI competition with us. And now the United States finally has acted.

Justice and Commerce Departments announced two days ago that the United States would cut off all access to these Chinese shell companies in Southeast Asia funneling these advanced semiconductors up into the Chinese market. That's a good decision. It's a late decision. It should have been done a year ago. And because of that decision, the Chinese foreign ministry spokesman said today - he said there could be Chinese countermeasures. So despite all of the good feeling President Xi meeting President Trump at the airport - which was really quite extraordinary - in Shenzhen, there's competition below the surface here. And I don't exclude the possibility of a mini trade war between the two, because China is always going to try to respond to what the United States has done.
FADEL: Now, President Trump also wants to focus on non-proliferation of nuclear weapons as China expands its weapons program. Is this something China wants to talk about?

BURNS: I think President Trump is right to raise it. This is - and - but China doesn't want to talk about it. China is engaged in the greatest buildup of its nuclear weapons force of any country in the world. And it's completely nontransparent. When I was ambassador in China, I raised the issue with them - as did others in our administration - and got nowhere. So the fact is that we're going to have a period of time in the 2030s when China and Russia will outweigh and outnumber the United States in nuclear weapons - strategic nuclear weapons.

This is the first time since the dawn of the nuclear age that will have happened. So I think the U.S. and our allies - Japan and the NATO allies - have to raise this with the Chinese and try to force them to be more transparent. I don't think that President Xi will agree to that today. But I do think that President Trump is right to raise the issue.
FADEL: Nicholas Burns, former U.S. ambassador to China, now at Harvard. Thank you for your time.

body_zh: 美国前大使谈特朗普与中国和俄罗斯领导人的联合峰会 NPR 的莱拉·法德尔 (Leila Fadel) 与美国前驻华和北约大使尼古拉斯·伯恩斯 (Nicholas Burns) 就特朗普总统计划与中国和俄罗斯领导人举行的会晤进行了交谈。
美国国家公共广播电台 (NPR) 的莱拉·法德尔 (Leila Fadel) 与美国前驻华和北约大使尼古拉斯·伯恩斯 (Nicholas Burns) 谈论了特朗普总统计划与中国和俄罗斯领导人会面的情况。
现在让我们转向尼古拉斯·伯恩斯。他曾担任拜登政府的美国驻华大使以及乔治·W·布什总统领导下的美国驻北约大使。他现在是哈佛大学的国际关系学者。早上好，大使。欢迎回到该计划。
尼古拉斯·伯恩斯：早上好，莱拉。谢谢。
法德尔：让我们从特朗普、习近平和俄罗斯总统普京之间的三方会晤开始。他们三人独家亮相，向美国盟友传递了什么信息？
伯恩斯：莱拉，我认为我们的盟友——日本、韩国、菲律宾、北约盟友——对这次会议非常担心。特朗普总统、习主席和普京总统在这里举行有史以来的首次会面。乌克兰也提上了议程——但乌克兰不在场。我认为没有泽伦斯基总统出席确实是一个重大错误。在这十年里，我们不能出现这样的情况：一个国家——乌克兰——的命运正在由另外三位领导人谈论，甚至可能决定。所以我认为美国把自己置于这样的境地是一个重大错误。
另一个应该坐在这张桌子上的国家是日本。去年，中国和俄罗斯对日本进行了大规模的恐吓行动——经济抵制、俄罗斯和中国在日本本土周围进行军事演习。日本是我们在亚洲的第一大盟友——但不是在谈判桌上。所以我认为这里的图像和拍照将成为本次会议的主要部分。这是一次短暂的会议。这对美国来说确实是错误的。我们的盟友对我们来说比中国和俄罗斯重要得多。
FADEL：当你说这是一个重大错误时，这个错误会带来什么后果？
伯恩斯：嗯，是盟友首都的焦虑和对美国失去信心。我特别认为，很多人都说这次会议有点像1945年2月的雅尔塔会议——斯大林、罗斯福、丘吉尔在东欧人的头上决定东欧的命运。 81年前和现在有很多不同。但事实上，当普京是侵略者而泽连斯基是受害者时，世界上三个非常强大的国家将讨论乌克兰应该发生什么，我认为这对于美国在北约联盟以及乌克兰人的信誉来说无疑是一个重大问题。
法德尔：我也想知道 - 我的意思是，中国在这里主办。但有些事情中国可能不想与美国讨论，其中包括最近对英伟达间谍活动的担忧。人工智能芯片的出口管制也更加严格。这将如何影响特朗普和习近平的会面？
伯恩斯：嗯，你知道，这就是房间里的大象，莱拉。特朗普总统已表示他不会提出这个问题。我确信习近平主席不会提出这个问题。但可以肯定的是，美国和中国之间将会在深圳就所发生的事情进行高层接触——间谍活动的指控，以及中国一直试图非法获取美国先进半导体以与我们进行人工智能竞争的事实。而现在美国终于行动了。

美国司法部和商务部两天前宣布，美国将切断这些中国在东南亚的空壳公司将这些先进半导体输送到中国市场的所有准入。这是一个很好的决定。这是一个迟到的决定。它应该在一年前就完成了。中国外交部发言人今天表示，由于这一决定，中国可能会采取反制措施。因此，尽管习近平主席在深圳机场会见特朗普总统的感觉非常好——这确实非常非同寻常——但这里却存在着潜在的竞争。我不排除两国之间爆发小型贸易战的可能性，因为中国总是会试图对美国的所作所为做出回应。
法德尔：现在，随着中国扩大其武器计划，特朗普总统还希望关注核武器不扩散问题。这是中方想谈的吗？
伯恩斯：我认为特朗普总统提出这个问题是正确的。这是——并且——但中国不想谈论它。中国正在世界上最大规模地建设核武器力量。而且它是完全不透明的。当我担任驻华大使时，我向他们提出了这个问题——就像我们政府中的其他人一样——但毫无结果。因此，事实是，到 2030 年代，中国和俄罗斯的核武器（战略核武器）数量将超过美国。
这是自核时代到来以来第一次发生这种情况。因此，我认为美国和我们的盟国——日本和北约盟国——必须向中国提出这个问题，并试图迫使他们变​​得更加透明。我认为习主席今天不会同意这一点。但我确实认为特朗普总统提出这个问题是正确的。
法德尔：尼古拉斯·伯恩斯，前美国驻华大使，现就读于哈佛大学。感谢您抽出时间。
